title: GS Yuasa stock heads toward November 6 results - AD HOC NEWS
content: GS Yuasa stock carries a JPY 572.6 billion market value as of October 7, 2026. Q1 revenue rose 7.5 percent and nine analysts set a JPY 7,000 target. GS Yuasa Corporation (ISIN JP3385820000) carried a market capitalization of JPY 572.6 billion on October 7, 2026, giving the Japanese battery maker a substantial valuation ahead of its next scheduled results. Its Tokyo-listed shares were last at JPY 5,708 at 3:30 p.m. JST, up 0.14 percent on the session. According to MarketScreener on September 21, 2026, revenue in fiscal Q1 2027 reached JPY 141.7 billion, up 7.5 percent from JPY 131.9 billion in the year-earlier quarter. Operating profit rose 39.3 percent to JPY 11.6 billion from JPY 8.3 billion, lifting the operating margin from 6.3 percent to 8.2 percent. Net profit increased 15.7 percent to JPY 7.6 billion from JPY 6.5 billion in the same comparison. MarketScreener attributed the operating improvement to pricing corrections, a more profitable sales mix and stronger overseas lead-acid battery volumes, while foreign-exchange losses and lower extraordinary income limited the bottom-line gain. Investing.com lists a Buy consensus from nine analysts, with eight Buy ratings and one Hold rating. The average 12-month target is JPY 7,000, while the highest target is JPY 8,200 and the lowest is JPY 5,300. Against the JPY 5,708 share price, the average target lies 22.6 percent above the price. The comparison matters because the stock remains below its JPY 7,899 52-week high, despite the latest operating-profit increase being more than four times the 7.5 percent revenue growth rate. GS Yuasa's investor-relations calendar lists November 6, 2026, for the results announcement covering the six months ended September 30, 2026. The same calendar also schedules a results briefing that day, giving investors the next formal checkpoint for pricing, battery volumes and margin progress. GS Yuasa stock was last at JPY 5,708 on the Tokyo Stock Exchange on October 7, 2026 at 3:30 p.m. JST. The session range was JPY 5,654 to JPY 5,779, while the 52-week range stood at JPY 3,532 to JPY 7,899.

title: GS Caltex Coach Targets Historic Two-Peat in New V-League Season - 조선일보
content: Coach Lee Young-taek seeks first back-to-back titles as V-League season begins on 31st “I will challenge to become the first coach in women’s volleyball history to achieve two consecutive championships (reign).” On the 7th, during the 2026-2027 V-League women’s division media day held at the Libera Hotel in Seoul’s Gangnam District, GS Caltex’s head coach Lee Young-taek stood on a podium one level higher than the other managers. While Heungkuk Life Insurance had previously won the championship finals in the 2005-2006 and 2006-2007 seasons consecutively, the head coaches who led those victories were different—Kim Cheol-yong and Hwang Hyun-joo. This is why Coach Lee expressed his determination to pursue the historic title. The seven teams in the V-League women’s division will participate in the NH Nonghyup Cup (final on the 18th) in Yeosu for a week starting on the 11th to assess their new season’s strength. The regular season will then begin on the 31st with a match between GS Caltex and Korea Expressway Corporation, kicking off a six-month-long campaign. GS Caltex and Korea Expressway Corporation, who faced each other in last season’s championship finals, are considered strong contenders for the title. Meanwhile, Heungkuk Life Insurance, under the leadership of head coach Yoshihara Tomoko in her second year, aims to reclaim the top spot. Hyundai Engineering & Construction, which recruited the ‘Indonesian star’ Megawati Pertiwi, is also evaluated as having the potential to challenge for the title. Industrial Bank of Korea (IBK), Jung Kwan Jang, and the newly established team SOOP Super, which struggled last season, are also preparing to rebuild their squads and aim for a leap to the upper ranks.

title: The Best Moments From Karol G’s Viajando Por El Mundo Tropitour - Rolling Stone
content: Karol G’s Viajando Por El Mundo Tropitour has been one hell of a spectacle this year. Since kicking off in July, the Colombian superstar has pulled out all of the stops with massive stage set-ups and high-production flares — and even some surprises. The show has even evolved to include a whole new section to highlight her latest album No Me Arrepiento de Sentir Tanto. With each new element — and star-studded surprise — Karol makes sure every night feels unique and exciting. We’ve compiled some of the best parts from her latest trek. By the time Karol launched her tour in Chicago, it was clear she was teasing something new. Fans at Soldier Stadium were treated to the official premiere of new song “Matadora” as a video of Karol dancing to the song appeared on the giant screens just as the show was over. It was a head-spinning way to start her Tropitour. Karol celebrated the announcement of No Me Arrepiento de Sentir Tanto with the live debut of one of the album’s most heartfelt cuts, “Si Lo Ven.” Wearing a white hoodie and bathed in blue light that bounced off her zip-up, the Colombian singer lamented a former flame — and had nearly all of Northwest Stadium tearing up. The evocative performance wasn’t just a tear-jerker moment, but a glimpse into the emotional landscape of her new project. Karol surprised fans at Sofi Stadium when she brought out Bruno Mars to perform their new collaboration “Still” for the very first time. The singer and pop hitmaker were a vision of romance as they serenaded each other, the stage lights perfectly glinting off their sequined outfits. Little did fans know that the performance would actually be a part of the “Still” music video — and that Mars’ presence was the start of an ongoing flirtation. Karol’s“BbY WOW” has been an unstoppable hit this year, and that’s partly thanks to Los Menor3s. The Venezuelan band sparked a viral trend on TikTok after they shared a video of themselves dancing to the track. At Karol’s tour stop in Massachusetts, the dance got its own onstage moment when the Colombian singer invited two of the three band members, Big Bowe and Sheba, to show off their inventive moves. “It was fun… It’s super random because we’re not dancers. What we do is make music, but we’re really grateful and happy that it happened,” Big Bowe told Remezcla. Karol continued to celebrate “BbY WOW” at her stop in New Jersey. On the first of two nights at MetLife Stadium, the singer transformed the show into an Ibiza club when she brought out the song’s collaborators Tainy, Spanish singer Judeline, and Spanish producer Rusowsky for the track’s explosive live debut. The trio performed from an elevated stage with the track’s superproducer, Tainy, spinning on a makeshift DJ table. Pink and blue strobes lit up the stadium, and fireworks even shot up into the sky, marking a true celebration of “BbY WOW” and its wild success. Karol delivered a surprise at the top of her second night at MetLife when she brought out Peso Pluma to perform their 2023 collaboration “QLONA.” “I want you to help me with a huge roar so we can sing this one with Peso Pluma,” Karol told the audience of 80,000 in Spanish. Of course, they obliged. It’s the second time this year that the duo have performed their sultry song together. The Mexican artist also joined Karol during her historic Coachella set for the final weekend, where she announced her Tropitour. When Becky G wrapped her final night as an opener, Karol made sure to celebrate the Mexican artist — and their close friendship. Before the two performed their 2022 collaboration “Mamii” for the last time on the Viajando Por El Mundo Tropitour, Karol surprised Becky with a giant bouquet of flowers. “Tonight is her last night with us. My heart is breaking, but we have had an incredible time. For me, she is like my other half on the stage,” Karol told the Jersey audience in Spanish. She then turned her attention to Becky: “I want to tell you that at the moment I called myself Karol G, there was a Becky G who was singing all over the world, making music all over the world. You were an inspiration for many of us. You were an inspiration, and you will continue to be an inspiration for me. Our stage is your home forever and ever.” The pair ended the sweet moment with a hug. Drake embodied his Champagne Papi persona when he joined Karol onstage in Houston to sing their new Spanish-language collaboration “Ahí” live for the first time. The pair leaned into the flirty energy of the track when Karol danced on Drake, and he yelled out, “Ay, que rico!” It was the first time they had shared the stage together, but Drake’s second time at the Tropitour; the rapper also attended Karol’s Toronto stop in July. Drake also treated Karol’s fans inside Reliant Stadium to a solo performance of his hits, “Janice STFU” and “One Dance.” Karol had a treat for fans in Miami: She brought out Eddy Lover to sing their Tropicoqueta collaboration “Dile Luna” together for the first time. The fun didn’t stop there. Karol asked the Panamanian artist to “sing [her] one more, the one that’s everyone’s favorite.” With that, Lover ripped through his reggaeton classic “Perdoname,” bringing Hard Rock Stadium right back to the 2000s and rousing the audience with each drum beat. The crowd proved that the song was, indeed, their favorite as they belted the chorus right along with Lover. Karol continued to show her love for Miami — and her opening acts — during her second night at Hard Rock Stadium when she had the night’s opener, Greeicy, perform their song “Amiga Mía” together, and then invited Elena Rose, who opened the night before, onstage as well. The Colombian singer handed both artists their own bouquets, just as she did with Becky G in New York. “I hope you both keep flourishing like these bouquets I brought you and that you keep being an inspiration for all of the women that are here tonight,” Karol told them. The trio of bichotas wrapped the sweet moment with a performance of Rose’s 2025 track “Orión.” It was the perfect embodiment of what Karol’s Tropitour is all about, being a proud Latina. title: UCT’s MASHA secures R14 million award to strengthen epidemic modelling - UCT News
content: The University of Cape Town’s (UCT) Modelling and Simulation Hub, Africa (MASHA) has joined a network of global leaders working to strengthen epidemic analytics and infectious disease modelling capacity across the Global South. It has secured a R14 million award through the newly launched Global South Leaders in Epidemic Analytics and Response Network (GS LEARN). The award positions MASHA as an implementing organisation in the global initiative, which was officially launched in Kigali, Rwanda on 22 and 23 September. MASHA will deliver the programme in partnership with the World Health Organization’s Immunization, Vaccines and Biologicals (WHO IVB) unit. Led by the Coalition for Epidemic Preparedness Innovations in partnership with the Gates Foundation and Global Health EDCTP3, GS LEARN aims to strengthen leadership, technical capacity and collaboration in epidemic analytics and infectious disease modelling across institutions in the Global South. According to Professor Sheetal Silal, the head of MASHA, the initiative addresses a critical need. “GS LEARN will fill a critical gap in epidemic and pandemic preparedness. By simultaneously increasing technical capacity in epidemic analytics and translational capacity among policymakers, we are laying the foundation for a global community that can anticipate threats and respond to outbreaks with locally grounded, data-driven decisions.” The initiative seeks to build locally led expertise through standardised training, mentorship, fellowships, work-based learning and long-term institutional partnerships. By expanding modelling capacity in regions most affected by infectious disease outbreaks, GS LEARN aims to ensure that expertise is available where it is needed to support immunisation policy, epidemic preparedness and outbreak response. The official launch brought together 35 participants from more than a dozen institutions across 11 countries, including regional facilitators, implementing institutions, participant organisations, funders and network partners. The two-day meeting marked the transition from programme planning to implementation and provided partners with an opportunity to align with GS LEARN’s vision, operational approach and collaborative priorities. Discussions focused on strengthening relationships between participating institutions and exploring how the network can support sustainable, locally led epidemic analytics capacity across regions. As part of the programme, three regional facilitating partners will coordinate activities across Africa, the Americas, and South and Southeast Asia. Professor Silal participated in the launch meeting and chaired a panel discussion on regional priorities and opportunities. The panel included representatives from GS LEARN’s regional facilitating partners: Africa CDC, the Pan American Health Organization, and the Indian Council of Medical Research’s National Institute of Epidemiology. Discussions explored regional gaps in epidemic analytics and modelling capacity, opportunities for collaboration, and ways in which GS LEARN can complement existing initiatives while strengthening locally led expertise. “We are laying the foundation for a global community that can anticipate threats and respond to outbreaks with locally grounded, data-driven decisions.” Silal also presented MASHA’s implementation plans for the programme, outlining the hub’s approach to training, mentorship, collaboration and engagement over the next three years. Through the award, MASHA will contribute to developing modelling literacy and strengthening leadership capacity among institutions across the Global South. The programme will support participants to interpret, contextualise and apply modelling evidence to inform immunisation decision-making, epidemic preparedness and outbreak response. The launch marks the beginning of GS LEARN’s implementation phase as participating institutions begin delivering activities across the network. Through its partnership with WHO IVB and the R14 million award, MASHA will play a key role in building sustainable modelling capacity and strengthening the institutional networks, skills and expertise required to support evidence-informed public health decision-making across the Global South. After finishing third in the regular league, his team demonstrated resilience by advancing to the postseason and clinching the title. This season, the treatment has changed. Lee sat in the top seat and threw out his challenge first. Many coaches have named GS Caltex as a championship contender. Lee joked, "Coming to Media Day with a championship title, I like the seating arrangement," drawing laughter. He then seriously stated, "Last season, we struggled through the regular league and won the championship in the postseason. We are determined to challenge again. Winning the championship has definitely changed how people view us. The players are overflowing with confidence. Once you win, you want to do it again. I know there is no team with two consecutive championships in the women's division. We will challenge for it." The dark horse team is Industrial Bank of Korea (IBK). With a strong roster and the addition of Japanese legend Manabe Minayoshi as head coach, Hyundai Engineering & Construction's Kang Sung-hyung and Lee Young-taek have both acknowledged IBK as a powerhouse. In response, Manabe said, "We have not even finalized our cup tournament roster yet. We plan to utilize as many players as possible," offering a cautious reply. Jung Kwan Jang's Kwon Soon-chan received the most spotlight. The team faced an unfortunate situation when head coach Ko Hee-jin abruptly resigned in August. After failing to find a replacement, the appointment was announced on the 6th, just a day before Media Day. Kwon introduced himself as a "second-day coach after meeting the team yesterday" and emphasized, "Our players' individual skills are not bad. However, the team's understanding of volleyball seemed lacking. There were many unforced errors. My task is to help the players express their abilities they have not yet shown." Among the players, intriguing stories abounded. First, Bukireechi and Mega, former teammates at Jung Kwan Jang, are now rivals. Bukireechi returned to Jung Kwan Jang after two seasons, while Mega, who played in Indonesia, rejoined Hyundai Engineering & Construction. Bukireechi declared, "I know Mega very well. I will definitely block him." Mega retorted, "As both of us are opposite spikers, will we even face each other? Of course, if we do, I will block him too." During their time at Jung Kwan Jang, Mega played as an outside hitter, but Hyundai Engineering & Construction plans to use her as an opposite spiker. Since they play the same position, they cannot directly face each other. The bond between GS Caltex's Silva, the league's top foreign player, and Heungkuk Life's rookie Kindelan was also noteworthy. Kindelan said, "As a fellow Cuban, I am proud of Silva. Watching her motivates me to do better." Silva responded, "I am honored to receive praise from a fellow Cuban. I am slightly older. (Laughs) Though we couldn't train together, it's touching and I appreciate it. I hope we can both show how strong Cuban players are on the court." title: Korean Conglomerate Heirs Favor Overseas Education; Columbia Leads - 조선일보
content: 93.9% of fourth- and fifth-gen owners studied abroad; Columbia University most attended overseas institution The overseas education patterns of South Korean conglomerate owner families are changing across generations. Up to the third generation, which includes Lee Jae-yong, chairman of Samsung Electronics, and Chung Eui-sun, chairman of Hyundai Motor Group, it was common to attend domestic universities before pursuing graduate studies, such as MBAs, abroad. However, among the fourth and fifth generations, cases of studying abroad from a young age or starting undergraduate studies directly at overseas universities have significantly increased. According to a survey by corporate data research firm CEO Score of 350 family members of owners from 89 major conglomerates, 46 out of 49 fourth- and fifth-generation owners (93.9%) had studied abroad. While only 5.9% of the first-generation founders had overseas education experience, the rate rose to 67.9% for the second generation and 78.7% for the third generation. Among the 46 fourth- and fifth-generation owners with overseas education experience, 33 (71.7%) began their undergraduate studies at foreign universities. For instance, Chung Hae-chan, the eldest son of Shinsegae Group Chairman Chung Yong-jin, and Seo Ho-jeong, the second daughter of Suh Kyung-bae, chairman of Amorepacific Group, both majored in hotel management at Cornell University in the U.S. Suh Min-jeong, the eldest daughter of Chairman Suh, studied economics at the same university. Lee Sun-ho, head of CJ Group’s Future Planning Division, studied financial economics at Columbia University in the U.S. Certain universities emerged as “frequent choices” for owner families. Four representatives from the fourth generation of GS Group—Heo Cheol-hong of GS Enttek, Heo Tae-hong of GS Futures, Hur Sae-hong of GS Caltex, and Hur Suh-hong of GS Retail—all graduated from Stanford University’s MBA program. At Doosan Group, five family members, including former chairman Park Yong-sung and Park Gee-won, chairman of Doosan Enerbility, completed their MBAs at New York University. Columbia University was the most attended overseas institution by owner families, with 22 individuals, including Shin Dong-bin, chairman of Lotte Group, and Shin Yoo-yeol, vice chairman of Lotte Holdings. This was followed by New York University (18), Cornell University (16), Stanford University (15), and Harvard University (14). Among domestic universities, Korea University had the highest number of owner family members at 54, followed by Seoul National University (50) and Yonsei University (35).

title: Will 30-Year US Treasury Yields Climb Higher? - Goldman Sachs

Long-term US Treasury yields will likely be under ongoing pressure amid elevated energy prices and subdued demand from institutional investors, says Muhammad Qubbaj, co-head of North America Interest Rate Product Sales and Trading at Goldman Sachs FICC and Equities. Thirty-year Treasury yields are trading around 5.7%, the highest since 2002. In the weeks ahead, energy prices are likely to be the key factor in longer-term interest rates, Qubbaj said in a webinar. Oil prices have risen this year due to the conflict in Iran, and the increase in energy prices will continue to pass through to other products even if crude stabilizes. Investors are cautious about locking in duration when rates could move even higher amid heavy bond issuance from the US government and other borrowers around the world. As tensions in the Middle East ripple through energy prices and inflation, they are also influencing the timing of the Federal Reserve’s next rate hike, how high its policy rate will ultimately climb, and the pressure investors exert on long-term Treasury yields, Qubbaj says. The factors driving up bond yields in the US are global in nature. Qubbaj says German and Japanese yields have risen together under the same three pressures: a higher policy path for rates, investors requiring more compensation to hold long-term bonds, and uncertainty over how much new debt can be absorbed at these levels. The Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting on September 15-16 provided several clear pieces of information for investors, Qubbaj says. The Fed coalesced around hiking rates twice this year. The first hike took place in September, and the second increase in rates will likely be in October or December, Qubbaj says. “That’s a timing debate, not an existence debate,” he adds. Bond investors, meanwhile, were positioned for a split decision from the FOMC. “We got consensus instead,” he says. “That alone was a repricing event.” At the same time, the committee said the rate increase was meant to remove a dose of accommodation. “In plain English, they don’t really think this is restrictive territory” for the economy, Qubbaj says.  “If you still see the policy rate as accommodative after hiking, September can’t have been one and done.” In addition, the committee communicated that the rate hike was in reaction to inflation running above the Fed’s target for years—not just according to recent economic data, Qubbaj says. The employment side of the Fed’s mandate, meanwhile, has largely been met. “They’re playing catch up, and that’s a durable motivation,” he says. The Fed also made clear that it is more focused on short-term yields than those on longer-maturity bonds. “The September meeting did something very, very important: It formally separated the front end from the long end,” Qubbaj says. “The Fed was very clear—it’s not going to police the long bond.” There is a “very clear implication” to this message, he says. “Hiking the front end doesn’t conjure up a bid for 30-year paper. The long end is going to have to find a yield that is attractive enough to bring in pensions and insurers. They are going to set the level, not the committee.” Even as the US government debt load grows, Qubbaj says the country’s debt-to-GDP ratio is not necessarily rising uncontrollably. Deficits of roughly 6% to 7% of GDP at a time when nominal growth is coming in at roughly 6% mean the deterioration is closer to around 1% per year. “That’s a drift, not a spiral,” Qubbaj says, adding that the US can plausibly grow into its debt without severe austerity. “I don’t think that’s priced” into the Treasury market, he says. “Sustainability and bond market clearing are different questions, and people conflate them.” While strong nominal growth can help stabilize the ratio of debt-to-GDP, how well the market can absorb the issuance of new Treasuries is a separate issue, Qubbaj says. Qubbaj says 30-year Treasury yields of 5.5% or higher are historically cheap, particularly in real, inflation-adjusted terms. A key question is whether there is a catalyst to push prices higher amid heavy supply, an uncertain inflationary backdrop, and cautious institutional buyers. “There is no clear catalyst” for 30-year Treasuries to rally, he says. Longer-term Treasuries typically yield some 50 to 100 basis points less than nominal GDP growth. With nominal growth of around 5%, there’s scope for the 30-year to rally to the point that its yield drops back down to 4.25%, Qubbaj says. But yields are not likely to fall back to 3% anytime soon. “To get something that low, you need a recession or a genuine growth shock, and that’s not on my bingo card right now,” he says. Georgia Southern University received approval from the Board of Regents of the University System of Georgia Tuesday to establish a Doctor of Optometry (O.D.) degree program. According to a release from the university, the decision authorizes the creation of Georgia’s first college of optometry at Georgia Southern and allows the institution to offer the new degree, filling a long-standing educational and health care gap in the state. The university anticipates enrolling an inaugural class in the O.D. program in Fall 2029. “This Doctor of Optometry program, the state’s first program of its kind, represents an important investment in health care education in Georgia by expanding regional health care access and removing geographic barriers for residents seeking optometric education and care,” said Avinandan Mukherjee, Ph.D., provost and executive vice president for academic affairs at Georgia Southern. “Building on a comprehensive health care education portfolio and interprofessional experiential pedagogies at Georgia Southern, this program will serve to expand access to ocular medicine while educating future Georgia optometrists.” The new college addresses a critical need for expanded access to eye care across the state, particularly in rural and underserved communities, and as an increased demand for modern, cost-effective eye care places new pressures on the health care system. By training future optometrists in Georgia, Georgia Southern will continue to help strengthen the health care workforce pipeline and improve health outcomes for generations to come, the release stated. The Regents approval also allows Georgia Southern to recruit an inaugural dean, followed by an associate dean, assistant dean and eventually several clinical and research directors, 25 specialized faculty members and 12 support staff. The degree approval follows the allocation of $29.8 million in direct state funding through the state’s Amended Fiscal Year 2026 Budget to launch the new college at Georgia Southern. The state investment supports the comprehensive renovation of the Highway 301 facility in Statesboro, converting it into a modern academic and clinical training center specifically tailored for optometric education. This resource also expands opportunities for students to pursue careers in vision care by exposing them to a new level and quality of academic preparation and clinical rotations that have not been available to them in the state of Georgia. The program is pending final approval by the Commission on Colleges and Universities and is in stage one of accreditation with the Accreditation Council on Optometric Education. In August, Georgia Southern announced that a Optometric Education Task Force, led by Horace Deal, O.D., was established to advise on the development of the University’s College of Optometry. Together, the task force will provide strategic guidance as Georgia Southern advances planning for the college of optometry, including program proposal, curriculum development, accreditation planning, partnerships, clinical education opportunities and workforce alignment.

title: New Omnivision GS HDR sensor advances next-gen industrial vision systems - Engineer Live
content: Semiconductor technology manufacturer Omnivision has launched a new 2.2-µm 5MP global shutter (GS) high dynamic range (HDR) CMOS image sensor that is purpose-built for industrial machine vision applications. Billed as an “industry first”, the OG5D GS sensor is suited for use in barcode scanners, factory automation, compact AI cameras and humanoid robots, especially data-collection devices for robotics training. “The rapid growth of industrial machine vision and robotics is driving demand for image sensors specifically designed for these emerging applications,” said Kelly Yan, staff product marketing manager at Omnivision. “Our new OG05D sensor delivers the ideal combination of compact size, high-speed imaging, excellent HDR performance and industry-leading low power consumption, enabling customers to build smaller, more capable and power-efficient industrial vision systems.” At a maximum output of 146 frames per second (fps) in linear mode, the new OG05D is 143% faster than previous-generation sensors. The sensor combines Nyxel near-infrared (NIR) technology, HDR, low power consumption and a compact optical format in a stacked backside-illuminated (BSI) sensor design. According to Omnivision, this combination delivers an optimised imaging solution for industrial and robotic vision systems where imaging performance, sensor size and power efficiency are essential. The OG05D GS sensor delivers HDR in a single exposure, reducing motion artifacts associated with multi-exposure HDR approaches. According to Omnivision, the sensor’s RGB-IR on-chip processing and imaging performance—combined with higher NIR quantum efficiency and low noise enabled by dual conversion gain—overcomes the challenges faces by traditional non-HDR sensors. The OG05D sensor comes in a 1/2.5-inch optical format and the package size is 6.6µm x 5.3µm, ideal for robotic, industrial and embedded AI camera designs. DCG HDR provides high-quality image capture across scenes containing both bright highlights and dark shadows. Enhanced HDR capability improves object detection and navigation in real-world situations where lighting conditions frequently change, including in factories, warehouses and the outdoors. title: Mikaela Shiffrin Plans Fewer Slaloms to Chase GS and Super-G - Ski Racing Media
content: Image Credit: “What’s the Point, Presented by Stifel” Mikaela Shiffrin plans to race fewer slaloms in 2026-27 and devote more training time to giant slalom and super-G. Her current plan calls for her first slalom start at Killington, followed by selected races through the winter. For the Stifel U.S. Ski Team athlete, the change begins with a question: Where does she most want to improve? In the video below, Shiffrin calls the coming winter an “exploration season.” After 16 years, she wants to give the disciplines that now spark her curiosity more room in her program. The decision follows a season in which she earned her ninth World Cup slalom title and reached 110 career World Cup victories. It changes how she will divide her training and racing time while she remains at the top of slalom. Shiffrin describes the moments that keep drawing her back to skiing: a turn that does not work, a conversation about why and the breakthrough that follows. Right now, GS and super-G offer the questions she most wants to answer. Last season, she says, she initially worried about losing her place among the top 30 in GS. Working back into the top seven showed her that she could find speed while still confronting fear. That experience helped renew her interest in what comes next. She wants dedicated training blocks to explore those possibilities, with fewer switches between disciplines. Slalom demands its own sustained preparation. Shiffrin says the coordination, reaction speed, physical effort and repetition require maximum attention. Reducing that training carries consequences, even for her. “One does not simply show up to any World Cup race and win,” she says. Under her current plan, Shiffrin would skip the early slaloms in Levi and Gurgl before returning to the discipline at Killington, Vermont, an Ikon Pass destination. She then intends to select additional slaloms. Maintaining her ranking matters because she wants the option to shift her focus again if she misses the discipline. The schedule also creates short windows for recovery and body maintenance. An early-season visit home could give her time with family and her new niece — an opportunity she rarely gets during the racing winter. Shiffrin cautions that her overall race load may look much the same once the season gets underway. The biggest difference could come in the first third of the winter, along with how she uses the time between races. Longevity runs through her explanation. Shiffrin says conversations after her Cortina injury helped her recognize that trying to do everything throughout an entire career might be unsustainable. Now she wants to see whether a different balance can help her continue doing the work she loves. “I’m not trying to do less because I care less,” she says. “I’m trying to do something different because I still care so much.” She acknowledges concern about disappointing fans and supporters. But she also says the people closest to her have encouraged her to choose what is best for her. Her plan leaves the outcome open. More focused training could reveal new possibilities in GS and super-G. Selected slalom starts could pull her back toward that discipline. title: ZXMoto is working BMW R1300 GS rivaling big-bore boxer twin - Visordown
content: ZXMoto has unveiled a working shaft drive boxer twin of around 1,000cc, with 100bhp. Two years after its founding, the Chinese brand is eyeing BMW's best-selling adventure bike. The burgeoning Chinese brand, ZXMoto, seems to be pushing in every available direction, with sports bikes, nakeds, lightweight off-roaders, rally bikes and more. If it’s got two wheels and an engine, ZXMoto wants to have a crack at building it. Its latest revelation, though, might see the brand going toe-to-toe with the biggest and best-selling adventure bike of the last twenty years. The company’s founder, Zhang Xue (hence the ‘ZX’ in the brand’s name), has revealed a new engine unlike anything in the existing range. Clearly a boxer twin, the company first teased the new engine at EICMA in 2025. Back then, it was nothing more than a rendering and a dream. Fast forward to today, and it’s fully designed and built, and seemingly ready to slot into a new bike. Presenting the engine at CIMA 2026, Zhang Xue showed off an apparently fully working and developed engine with a capacity of around 1,000cc. While the official specification of the engine remains unknown at the time of writing, reports from China suggest it has an output north of 100bhp, liquid cooling, and chain-driven cams, as per the latest generation of boxer twins from BMW. Like the BMW engine, the ZXMoto powerplant features a longitudinal layout, with an output shaft at the rear of the engine. That is obviously priming it for a shaft drive to the rear wheel, a feature that has become a mainstay of BMW’s sports touring and adventure bikes. And while a boxer twin of around 1,000cc and more than 100bhp isn’t groundbreaking in itself, it’s the speed of development that is the more interesting part of this story. ZXMoto was only officially founded in 2024. By 2025, it was presenting new bikes at EICMA, racing, and winning in the WorldSSP championship, while also showing off new engines and technologies. Now, just two years after the company was formed, it has a working large-capacity boxer twin that appears to be designed with a shaft-driven motorcycle in mind. That is a fairly clear statement of intent. There is also the question of what happens next. ZXMoto has shown that it can move from an idea to a production-ready engine remarkably quickly, and a boxer twin opens up more possibilities than just one adventure bike. A shaft-driven sport tourer, road bike or even a large-capacity naked could all make use of the same basic powerplant. What we do know is that the company has gone from showing a computer-generated boxer twin at EICMA 2025 to displaying a working engine at CIMA 2026. The idea here is that analysts revising their estimates right before an earnings release have the latest information, which could potentially be more accurate than what they and others contributing to the consensus had predicted earlier. title: Unpopular Opinion: Karol G’s Karol G Tropitour Was for the Latina Who Cried Through ‘Mañana Será Bonito’ and Needed to Know She Made It Through - BELatina
content:
The Karol G Viajando por el Mundo Tropitour concert in Miami almost did not happen for me, and I say that knowing full well how different this story would feel if it had not. An opportunity came through Acoustyle and I decided to take it, bringing my Colombian friend Angélica Romero along, a paisa from Medellín and a costeña from Barranquilla navigating the aggressively humid Miami streets together on a night that turned out to be a lot more than either of us had anticipated. The heat that greeted us outside was the type that slaps you across the face and reminds you exactly where you are, and somehow it was perfect because we were already feeling tropical before we even walked through the doors, already carrying that specific electricity that comes from being two Colombian women about to watch a Colombian woman own a stage. It is worth being honest about the hesitation that many Karol G fans felt going into the Tropitour era, because I felt it too. After Mañana Sera Bonito, which functioned as collective healing for women in a way that felt less like a concert and more like therapy, some of us were still craving that specific hug from her music, the one that spoke directly to the broken parts of Latinas and made us feel seen in our pain. Tropicoqueta is a different energy, and at first that difference felt disorienting, like being handed something bright and colorful when part of you was still holding on to something tender. But standing in that crowd in Miami, sweating through a sexy outfit, holding a cold drink dripping down my arm while singing every word, I understood it completely. Latinas are multifaceted, and we are not always in our healing era. Sometimes we are in our tropical, fully alive era, and Karol G was giving us permission to inhabit that version of ourselves without guilt or apology. To understand what the Tropitour meant to me, you have to understand what Mañana Sera Bonito did to me first. That era saved me in ways I am still processing, arriving during one of the hardest periods of my life, a year where everything felt so heavy that I genuinely was not sure I was going to make it through emotionally. Karol G’s voice was on repeat constantly, and I was praying and daydreaming for a day when I would feel whole again, playing her album like a promise I was making to myself that the day would come. The fact that she is Colombian, from Medellín, the same city as me, made her feel like a sister in those moments, like someone who understood without needing to be told, and that closeness carried me through more dark nights than I want to count. Because the album meant so much to me, I made it a point to join her Mañana Sera Bonito show in Miami, putting on the sparkles, getting all cute and walking into Hard Rock Stadium with a heavy heart but ready to be there for every second of it. Music has a way of creating intimacy with people you will probably never meet, and sometimes a voice and a melody is proximity enough to make you feel less alone in what you are going through, which is exactly what that night was supposed to be for me. But when “Amargura” came on and I felt everything in my chest rise to the surface at once, I slipped out of my seat and let the moment pass without me, protecting myself from a grief I was not ready to feel in public. I carried that unfinished feeling without even knowing it was still there, tucked underneath everything else, waiting for the right moment to finally let it breathe. When Karol G came out at the Tropitour, her energy moved through the crowd before I even had time to prepare myself for it, and the next thing I knew I was fully in it, moving and singing and feeling every bit of the tropical night she had built around us, the version of myself from the Mañana Sera Bonito era feeling very far away in the best possible sense. She moved through her original songs before inviting people onto the stage to dance with her, including two Cubans she mentioned were among the first Cubans she had ever brought on stage, a Mexican and two Colombians, and there was something about watching all of us come together in that moment for a good perreo to “Bby Wow” that felt like a celebration of everything live music is supposed to be, a room full of people from different places finding the same joy at the same time. What made it even more special was that she incorporated TikTok videos of fans doing the Bby Wow trend into the show, which said everything about how she and her team operate because they are genuinely paying attention to what is happening around her influence and they are choosing to honor it rather than take it for granted, and that attentiveness is one of the things that separates Karol G from artists who simply perform for their audience rather than with them. That same spirit showed up when she brought out mariachis, then Elena Rose and Greeicy, giving the stage to artists who are still building their moment in a way that not every artist at her level chooses to do, and watching her create space for others when she has worked so hard to create space for herself felt like its own lesson. By the time she performed “Bichota” with cumbia influences, the song felt like it had grown alongside everyone in that crowd, like we were all moving closer to our folkloric roots together, because somewhere underneath all the perreo we have always been craving that sound and the Tropitour feels like Karol G’s way of telling us we are allowed to want it all. In the middle of the concert, the flames going off next to us were adding an extra layer of heat to an already sweltering night when “Amargura” came on. I heard the first few notes and my body knew before my brain did, and everything I had been carrying from the last time I heard that song live came rushing back in an instant. The last time I had heard it live I had to leave the room because I was not ready for what it was going to bring out of me, and this time I stayed, sang every word, danced to it and let myself feel joy inside a song that once felt too heavy to inhabit, and somewhere in the middle of all of that I realized that the unfinished moment I had been carrying since the Mañana Sera Bonito tour had finally been completed. It was the full circle I did not know I was walking toward when I almost skipped this concert entirely. Karol G moves through eras constantly but she is someone whose music always accounts for what is in your heart and walks alongside you whether you are broken or thriving or somewhere in the complicated space between the two, and the Tropitour is proof that she has never stopped doing that even as the sound has changed. We can be emotional bichotas with a matadora energy and still have time to sing “Pineapple” and “Mamiii” because we contain all of it, and Karol G has been telling us that unapologetically through every genre she touches. Standing in that crowd in Miami, finally singing “Amargura” without having to leave the room, I understood that the healing she started with me during Mañana Sera Bonito was never really over.
